ai.instructions:
- Amplenote must be running with its MCP server turned on. If a tool says the server isn't reachable or the token was rejected, tell the user exactly that.
- Use search-notes to find notes and get-note to read one. Never invent noteUUIDs or taskUUIDs; always take them from tool results.
- Pass includeBacklinks to get-note when the user asks which notes mention or link to a note, such as a person or project.
- search-tasks defaults to all open tasks. Use view=overdue, today, upcoming, or unscheduled for those groups, and view=completed for recently completed tasks.
- add-task adds to today's Daily Jot unless the user names a note. Pass the exact note name from search-notes as noteName.
- Use append-to-note to jot down notes, ideas, or several lines of text; it defaults to today's Daily Jot. Use add-task for a single task with dates or priority.
- Use get-note-tasks for the tasks of one specific note; search-tasks only covers notes in task domains.
- If add-task returns inTaskDomain: false, tell the user the task was added but will not appear in task lists until the note is added to a task domain in Amplenote. null means it could not be checked; do not mention it then.
- Convert relative dates like "tomorrow" or "next Monday" to YYYY-MM-DD before passing startDate or deadline. If you are not sure what today is, call get-daily-jot first; it returns today's date, weekday, and time zone.
- For questions about a Daily Jot ("what did I jot down yesterday?"), call get-daily-jot with daysFromToday, then get-note with its noteUUID.
- A task is overdue when its deadline has passed. To reschedule an overdue task, move its deadline with update-task (and its startDate too if it has one).
- complete-task can be undone with reopen-task.
- Summarize results instead of dumping long lists or whole notes into the chat.
